page: The Vultr voc-s-32c-256gb-5760s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC processors. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, and BMI2.

Resource allocation features a substantial 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive operations. Local storage consists of a built-in 5760 GB NVMe SSD, delivering high-density high-throughput local disk capacity without external block storage attachments. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory throughput, recording 515.15 GB/sec on large-block read operations and 253.87 GB/sec on large-block writes, both placing in the top decile of tested systems. Multi-core performance is solid, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 63,855.09 and a stress-ng multi-core measurement of 99,520.25. In-memory data store performance is similarly strong, achieving 70.76 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, general integer and web-serving workloads, such as static web throughput (27.73 GB/sec) and Geekbench single-core execution (1776.0), perform within median tiers.

Given the bundled 5.76 TB NVMe disk footprint, generous memory allocation, and top-tier RAM bandwidth, this server configuration offers balanced hardware cost efficiency for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, compilation clusters, and data-intensive ETL pipelines that require consistent I/O and dedicated CPU time.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture without hardware GPU acceleration, it maintains an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio paired with high-capacity local disk space. Benchmark results indicate exceptional large-block memory bandwidth exceeding 515 GB/sec for reads and 253 GB/sec for writes, alongside strong multi-core compute metrics such as 99,520.25 in stress-ng and 70.76 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread execution rates remain in average tiers, its dedicated vCPU profile, combined with ample memory and fast local NVMe storage, delivers strong qualitative resource efficiency for memory-heavy databases, caching engines, and large-scale data ingestion workflows.
